question: The open finding of p3_startup_2026-09-26.json: a fresh detector started at the gate's piece-2 cut (new_data_55_0013, a standing train) STOPs on frames 12-15 at 2.9-3.1 m on a `low` track made of the rail heads 3.0-3.6 m ahead, 3-12 cm above the young model's rail-head plane, in front of the 4-30 m range the bed cross-section is learned from. Rule c (tracking.low_min_seen_distance 4 m) removed it but opened a blind zone (17 of 40 ray-cast cases: the organizers' 0.3 x 0.3 x 0.1 m object and an object lying across a rail 3.0-3.9 m ahead of a standing or slow train never STOP). Is there a narrow rule that removes the rail-head STOP and keeps every blind-zone case a STOP?

preregistered.before_any_result: No candidate code exists and no candidate was run. Known before this file, all with the shipped defaults (no rule): (1) the reproduction below; (2) one instrumented replay of the finding printing every low cluster under 4.5 m with the features the candidates use; (3) the 40-case ray-cast set of addendum_blind_zone rebuilt as an agent scratch script (blind_zone.py: resense.synthetic.synthetic_tunnel_frame, noise seeds 0-4 cycled, the 0.5 m box and the object lying across a rail standing on the bed at z = -1.5, the organizers' object on the rail head at z = -1.32): with the defaults it gives the recorded rule-off result in 40 of 40 cases (STOP yes / no, first STOP frame, STOP frame count; 32 cases STOP), and the same features printed for its objects at 3.0 / 3.5 / 3.9 m.

features_measured_before.definition: per low cluster under 4 m: band = its lateral extent [dy_min, dy_max] (its own points); top = the highest return of the frame (any stage, h in -0.3 ... 0.6 m above the modelled rail head) in the band within the cluster's along-track extent; ref = the median over 0.25 m along-track bins (>= 2 returns) between gauge.range_min - 0.5 = 2.5 m and 6.0 m, outside the cluster's extent +- 0.3 m, of the highest return of the band in the bin: the height of the structure the cluster sits in where the cluster is not; diff = top - ref
features_measured_before.finding: every low cluster under 4 m of the 40 frames (15 clusters, the finding's track 12 on frames 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 included): diff 0.010-0.037 m, ref 0.135-0.148 m (the rail head stands 14-17 cm above the young model's plane at 2.7-6 m), 6-12 reference bins, width 0.15-0.39 m, the band overlaps an expected rail line (+-rails_spacing/2 = +-0.795 m from the model axis) +- 0.10 m in all
features_measured_before.raycast_objects: the organizers' object on a rail head at 3.0 / 3.5 / 3.9 m (fresh and moving): diff 0.100-0.108 m, width 0.30-0.31 m; the object lying across a rail: diff 0.131-0.140 m, width 0.54-0.60 m; the 0.5 m box across a rail at 3.9 m (its low cluster): diff 0.318-0.321 m, width 0.50-0.51 m; ref 0.002-0.006 m (the synthetic model is right); the empty tunnel has no low cluster under 8 m

C1.rule: A low cluster (kind 'low') is marked rail geometry when (1) it starts nearer than rail_start_within (4.0 m = lowobj.template_range[0], where the bed cross-section starts being learned); (2) its lateral extent reaches an expected rail line (the model axis +- track.rails_spacing / 2) within rail_start_lateral; (3) it is at most rail_start_max_width wide across the track (an object lying across a rail is wider); (4) the same lateral band continues along the track: at least 4 of the 0.25 m bins between 2.5 m and rail_start_within + 2 m, outside its extent +- 0.3 m, hold >= 2 returns (it is a piece of a structure elongated along the track, not a compact object); and (5) its top (the band's highest return within its extent, corridor points above the envelope floor included) is at most rail_start_margin above ref, the band's height where the cluster is not (the rail head's own returns): at rail-head height, nothing standing on it. The tracker does not newly report a low track whose cluster of this frame is marked and that was never matched at or beyond rail_start_within; a track already reported, or once matched at >= 4 m (a real object approached from afar: set O's low objects are first matched at >= 10 m), is not affected. The association, the tracks and every other stage are unchanged, so the rule can only withhold a report: never add a STOP, never delay a STOP of an unmarked track.
C1.why_narrow: the finding's clusters are rail-head flank returns 1-4 cm under the rail head's own line (diff <= 0.037 m); a real object on a rail rises above that line (the organizers' 0.10 m object: diff >= 0.100 m), an object lying across a rail is wider than 0.45 m and rises above it; objects lying along a rail at rail-head height stay the documented limitation (ALGORITHM section 6) and are unchanged beyond 4 m

C2.rule: C1 with a tighter margin and width (more room for a real object, less for the rail); run only if C1 fails S2 or S3
